issue.title: test_capacity_gate_to_admission: land segment has queue_weight None where tests expect 2.0 (2 nodes fail at master 244442ee8)
issue.description:
Two tests in tests/test_capacity_gate_to_admission.py fail deterministically at master
244442ee8: test_epic_gate_capacity_reaches_weighted_admission (assert land.queue_weight
== 2.0, got None, line 152) and test_omitted_capacity_preserves_land_weight_and_global_budget
(same None-vs-2.0 assertion shape). The rendered `bd/land_epic` segment expands to
PromptDirectives with queue_weight=None and queue_weight_explicit unset, i.e. the land
segment carries no explicit queue weight when the test expects one.

Found 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_31 while verifying an unrelated change; the
test-scoped lane failed on these two nodes and they fail with the node run alone (~3s).

Attribution attempted, not resolved: run per commit in a detached worktree with
PYTHONPATH pointing at it, the failure is present at 244442ee8, 9cfb06a54, 9231c9352,
65c8169f9 and e65cc22ee, so it predates the five most recent commits; the test file was
last touched by 89d51301f ("feat: adopt queue capacity budget adapters"). The six
sase-core commits between the pinned sase-core-revision.txt and the linked checkout used
by this workspace's build (tool-run fingerprints, fleet catalog, gateway capability) do
not touch queue weights, so core skew is unlikely but not excluded. It is also not ruled
out that the workspace's installed plugins or user xprompt config change how
bd/land_epic expands; whoever picks this up should first confirm it reproduces on a
clean CI checkout, then find where the land directive's queue weight is supposed to be
applied (%queue directive wiring landed in 0770357cd).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails on every run and alone (~3s), and at all five most recent commits checked in detached worktrees; the assertion is a fixed None-vs-2.0 comparison with no timing or ordering dependence. A rerun on the same tree never passed.
